title: Sequential fleet surgery for throughput-stable maintenance
creator: Maya Patel
description: We need an automated, low-risk maintenance pattern for Dedicated fleets that preserves throughput SLAs during node lifecycle events (drain, upgrade, reprovision). Current rolling drains occasionally cause transient throughput drops when shard placement and KV cache warmup lag behind re-routing. This ticket implements a 'sequential fleet surgery' orchestrator that performs coordinated per-zone node maintenance with pre-warm, capacity reservations, probe traffic, and automated rollback to avoid customer-facing degradation.
problem_statement: Uncoordinated drains and upgrades can cause 10-30% throughput variance for affected customers for up to several minutes. Manual staging is error-prone and scales poorly as fleet size grows and regions expand. We need an automated approach that guarantees throughput floors during maintenance windows and integrates with autoscaling policies.
proposed_solution: Implement a Fleet Surgery Orchestrator that performs maintenance in controlled micro-windows: 1) Reserve throughput tokens for affected routes (safety buffer), 2) Select candidate nodes using placement heuristics (load, shard locality, KV cache hit rates), 3) Launch pre-warm helper nodes and replicate KV caches ahead of drain, 4) Shift a small fraction of traffic as probe traffic to validate behavior, 5) Execute drain with graceful in-flight migration and pause of non-critical background work, 6) Validate post-drain metrics and either commit upgrade or perform automated rollback. Orchestrator exposes policies: max_concurrent_nodes, throughput_reservation_pct, prewarm_timeout, probe_traffic_pct, and maintenance_window SLA targets.
design_notes:
- Use existing routing layer hooks to atomically apply throughput reservations per-route before node evacuations.
- Extend KV cache manager to support on-demand snapshot + incremental sync for warmup on target nodes.
- Integrate with autoscaler to avoid triggering scale down during surgery; autoscaler should treat reserved tokens as temporary demand.
- Provide a dry-run mode that simulates surgery and emits a report of expected throughput impact.
- Store surgery manifests in control-plane db so rollbacks can reference pre-surgery routing state.
- Expose surgery progress and rollback actions in Console with per-customer visibility for Dedicated tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can run a staged drain across a three-AZ cluster without violating a 95% throughput floor for P1 customers in 9/10 simulated runs
Prewarm kicks off and achieves >=80% KV cache hit rate on target node before traffic shift within configured prewarm_timeout
Autoscaler respects throughput reservations and does not scale down reserved capacity during active surgery
Console shows surgery step-by-step progress and allows operator-initiated abort and rollback
Add E2E test harness that can simulate node failures and verify automated rollback within 2 minutes when post-drain error rate exceeds threshold

risks: Prewarm may not reach sufficient cache hit rates for large models within reasonable time; helper node cost is non-trivial and must be bounded. Autoscaler integration complexity could delay rollout. Improper reservation sizing could starve other tenants if misconfigured.
mitigations:
- Limit concurrent surgeries per-fleet and per-region.
- Default conservative reservation_pct (5%) with gradual ramp.
- Charge helper node time to maintenance budget and expose estimated cost before run.
- Add circuit-breaker to abort surgery if probe error rates cross threshold.
- Run progressive canaries on small customer cohorts before fleet-wide enablement.
implementation_notes: Prefer feature-flagged rollout: start with dry-run & telemetry, then enable prewarm + probe traffic on test fleets, then expand to small subset of Dedicated customers. Coordinate calendar maintenance windows with Sales for impacted Dedicated tenants. Ensure runbook includes manual escalation path to drain or evict surgery manifest.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for routing reservations and drain state transitions. 2) Integration tests with KV sync in a multi-node emulated cluster. 3) Load tests with pegged generator to validate throughput floor. 4) Failure injection tests to validate automated rollback. 5) Console acceptance tests for visibility and controls.
notes_for_release: Document maintenance cost implications and default policy values in the Dedicated admin guide. Announce opt-in pilot to early customers and schedule partner support rotation during first wave of surgeries.
estimated_implementation_effort: 3 engineers x 6 sprints (parallelized across routing, KV, autoscaler)
